text:
Jackson LaCombe is playing 26:17 a night, and at 25 he has turned into Anaheim's do-everything defenseman. He has 27 points in 26 games, all but one of them assists, and 17 on the power play, where he's on the ice for 83% of his team's chances (65% last season). That's a real breakout in role: 1.04 points a game, up from 0.71.

The points are louder than the play, though. At even strength, the Ducks have just 39.68% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with LaCombe on the ice, almost ten points worse than when he sits. And Anaheim has scored 7.8 more goals than its chances deserve with him out there, which flatters his assist total. Evolving-Hockey liked his play-driving last season, 94th percentile among defensemen, so this may be the cost of huge minutes against top lines. Our numbers project 72 points. Watch the even-strength share; that's where his season gets decided.
headline: Jackson LaCombe has become the Ducks' everything
